description: We are Team Mars, participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are working on the SPHEREx challenge, aiming to develop a tool that helps users explore repeated sky observations and identify moving objects over time. Our interests include astronomy, Python, AI, image processing, and data analysis. We welcome motivated and creative teammates who are passionate about space science and technology.
summary:
SKYTRACE is an interactive web platform that transforms real NASA SPHEREx infrared observations into an engaging, time-based sky exploration experience. It allows users to select a region of the sky and explore its observations across different times and infrared wavelengths using interactive Blink, Compare, and Difference modes.

The platform provides two exploration experiences: Scientific View, which presents original observations, metadata, measurements, and orbital information using NASA JPL Horizons; and Simple View, which helps users understand the journey of celestial objects through clear visual explanations. Users can explore examples such as Vesta, 3I/ATLAS, Mira, and Barnard’s Star.

SKYTRACE addresses the challenge of making complex astronomical data easier to access, compare, and understand. By connecting real observations with scientific context, it supports students, educators, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers in exploring changes in the sky.

Our core principle is: **Investigate changes, not confirm discoveries.**
details:
Project Details – SKYTRACE

SKYTRACE is an interactive web platform that transforms NASA SPHEREx observations into an accessible, time-based sky exploration experience. Inspired by the search for Planet X, it helps users navigate astronomical data, visualize observations, and investigate how the sky changes over time.

Users can begin by entering sky coordinates, selecting a suggested target, following a guided story, or choosing a location on an interactive sky map. They can explore available observations and compare images from different times using playback, side-by-side comparison, and difference views. These tools help users investigate potential movement and brightness variations without claiming or confirming astronomical discoveries.

The platform offers two exploration experiences: Scientific View, which provides access to original observations, metadata, measurements, and orbital information through NASA JPL Horizons; and Simple View, which presents the journey of celestial objects through real stars, constellations, and the Milky Way, while distinguishing past observations from future predictions.

Our project benefits students, educators, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers by making complex infrared observations easier to access and understand. Its intended impact is to encourage scientific curiosity, support astronomy education, and provide an accessible starting point for investigating real astronomical data without requiring advanced programming skills.

We developed the frontend using Next.js, React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. The backend uses Python and FastAPI for observation searches and image retrieval. The interactive sky navigator uses Aladin Lite, with DSS optical imagery providing navigation context. Real SPHEREx observations are accessed through NASA/IPAC IRSA, while orbital information is obtained through NASA JPL Horizons. We used Visual Studio Code for development and GitHub for collaboration and version control.

In addition, our image-processing workflow uses Python in Jupyter Notebook, together with Astropy, Reproject, and Photutils. We inspected FITS image data and World Coordinate System (WCS) information, reprojected observations onto a common reference grid, evaluated image overlap, and analyzed astronomical sources to assess alignment accuracy. This processing helps establish a more reliable basis for comparing observations taken at different times.

SKYTRACE's creativity lies in combining a cinematic space interface with practical scientific exploration tools. It brings together time-based image comparison, interactive sky navigation, guided astronomical stories, and scientific context in one platform, making complex observations more approachable for different audiences.

Throughout development, our team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, navigation, loading performance, image alignment, consistent brightness, and comparable observation bands. We clearly distinguish synthetic demonstration data from real SPHEREx observations, and optical navigation imagery from infrared scientific data. We also distinguish observed positions from future orbital predictions and communicate uncertainty responsibly.

Our guiding principle is: Investigate changes, not confirm discoveries. SKYTRACE empowers people to explore astronomical evidence, ask questions, and investigate what may be happening in the sky.
